The Zimbabwean man was arrested on November 8 at a Johannesburg airport while attempting to board a flight to Russia.
A South African court has convicted and sentenced a Zimbabwean man for trying to travel to Russia to fight in Ukraine after he was arrested earlier this month alongside eight others.
Tafadzwa Sithole was sentenced to five years in prison on Tuesday, under a five-year suspension, meaning he would only have to serve the time if he is convicted of a similar crime within that time period. Sithole is set to be deported back to Zimbabwe.
He told the court that he had agreed to fight for Russia in the war in exchange for “remuneration” after successfully applying online in Zimbabwe.
“He knew that the Russian Federation was engaged in an ongoing armed conflict with Ukraine and that the military service he intended to render would be performed in the context of that armed conflict,” his lawyer told the court.
Sithole was arrested at OR Tambo international airport on November 8 while attempting to board a flight to Russia.
Sithole said a person he identified as “Albina” contacted him after he submitted the application, arranged accommodation in South Africa and provided a flight ticket to Russia. His admissions were detailed in a plea agreement with South African prosecutors.
He pleaded guilty to violating the Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act. The act prohibits mercenary activity and regulates military assistance to parties in foreign conflicts, including recruitment and training, and also applies to foreign nationals.
Sithole, who described himself as an unemployed third-year student at a university in Zimbabwe, appeared in court with four other accused who are also negotiating plea agreements with prosecutors.
He said he entered South Africa legally on November 4 and stayed in an accommodation in Kempton Park, east of Johannesburg, in preparation for his travel to Russia.
Zimbabwe is among several African countries where Russia has been recruiting fighters for its war against Ukraine. Others include South Africa, Kenya, Botswana and Ghana.
Zimbabwean authorities said in March that 15 citizens had been killed in the war in Ukraine and that they were seeking the return of 66 others. The government said recruits were promised well-paid jobs but had their travel documents confiscated and were forced into combat.
Kenya ’s government said in February that more than 1,000 citizens had been recruited to fight for Russia. Families protested in Nairobi in March, demanding their relatives’ return and the prosecution of those responsible.
An investigation by Code for Africa, a nonprofit data journalism and technology organisation, identified 289 websites, domains and social media profiles used to lure recruits through false advertising and promises of generous benefits.

Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi.
The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially said he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy.
Sarkozy was given a five-year sentence in the case last September and became the first French ex-president to go to jail, even though he only spent 20 days behind bars. He has always denied doing anything wrong in the case and the appeals verdict is expected next Monday.
Since losing his re-election bid in 2012, Sarkozy has faced several criminal investigations.
In 2024, he was handed a one-year sentence – of which six months were suspended – over the illegal financing of his 2012 re-election campaign.
In 2021, he was found guilty of trying to bribe a judge and sentenced to three years in jail – two of them suspended – and thus became the first former French president to get a custodial sentence. He was allowed to serve his time at home wearing a tag instead of going to jail.
The new case centres on a Libyan businessman, Ziad Takieddine, who had said he had written proof that Sarkozy's 2007 campaign bid was "abundantly" financed by Tripoli, and that the €50m (£43m) in payments continued after he became president.
Takieddine, who died last year, withdrew his accusations in an interview in 2020.
At the time, Sarkozy was said to have stated: the "truth is finally coming out", but officials found the retraction to be "insincere" and a new investigation was launched into the "Save Sarko" file – the nickname the alleged perpetrators had used for the operation, according to French media.
So the former head of state and his wife, an Italian-born former supermodel and singer, will now face charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" and benefiting from witness tampering. They deny any wrongdoing.

Nicolas Sarkozy illegal campaign financing conviction upheld

US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation.
Blanche said he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.
Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
Asked several times on Tuesday if the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about."
Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged China spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia.
Trump has said he would consider pardoning Huang for any potential criminal activity, though he does not think it will come to that.
"It's always an option, I guess, but I don't think it'll be necessary," Trump told the New York Post in an interview published on Tuesday.
The US commerce department has also announced it was preparing to blacklist the tech company Megaspeed, which has been suspected of helping to divert advanced chips to China.
In a joint statement last week, the commerce and justice departments said they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations" .
But speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Blanche said the latter department has "hundreds, if not more" export investigations occurring at any one time.
"So when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about," he said.
Asked if he was satisfied Nvidia had been co-operative with any efforts to get to the bottom of whether the company or Huang potentially knew about any chips being diverted to China, Blanche said: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.
"Obviously, if Nvidia was the target or was subject to some criminal investigation or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people.
While Nvidia's stock market value surged on the announcement of Huang's reappointment, some of the gains were reversed in volatile Tuesday trading.
The company's share price closed down nearly 6% - still well above where it ended last week. On Monday, Nvidia stock rocketed more than 31% following news of Huang's return.
Huang reportedly apologised to Nvidia employees on Tuesday, the day after returning to the company as chief executive, saying he made "terrible mistakes" and is now in therapy for 90 minutes per day.
The company's board reinstated Huang on Monday in a shock U-turn. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, said Huang's return was in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".
The board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.
On Monday, Trump said he spoke to the company's directors and convinced them to bring back Huang .
Republican congressman Don Bacon said Nvidia should have "ignored the Administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang".
Republican Senator Pete Ricketts said Huang's behaviour "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips".
Democratic congressman Robert Garcia, the incoming chairman of the House oversight committee, said Trump's "direct involvement" with Nvidia's decision "raises serious national security and corruption questions".
Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego said Congress needed to "investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement".
US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund. UEFA Champions League Round 1.
Match report as Arsenal are denied victory by Borussia Dortmund in a Champions League encounter at the Emirates Stadium; Viktor Gyokeres scored a spectacular opener but Maximilian Beier equalised as the Gunners wasted a string of chances
Arsenal were punished for failing to take their chances for the second game in a row as Maximilian Beier clinched a 1-1 draw for Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.
Viktor Gyokeres gave Arsenal an early lead with a stunning strike from distance but the game followed a similar pattern to Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle as they were unable to capitalise on a one-sided first half before conceding after the break.
Dortmund's leveller came when Beier slotted a clinical finish past Kepa Arrizabalaga, standing in for the injured David Raya, following a rampaging run from defender Joane Gadou.
Arsenal racked up 30 shots and had a string of chances to win it in the closing stages, hitting the woodwork through Jurrien Timber's deflected cut-back and again through Declan Rice's low shot.
Gyokeres also spurned opportunities, firing over from close range from Martin Odegaard's pass shortly before half-time, then heading awkwardly wide from a few yards out when it looked easier to score from another Odegaard ball.
Dortmund had dangerous moments too, including a Jobe Bellingham goal ruled out for offside and a penalty appeal for a handball by Gyokeres following a corner.
Arsenal remain unbeaten in the Champions League but the draw causes them to drop two places in the league phase table to fifth before they resume their Premier League campaign at home to Manchester City, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.
Arsenal's total of 30 shots was their highest in the Champions League either this season or last. But only one of them ended up in the net. Only four of them were even on target.
There were clear parallels with Saturday's game at St James' Park. Again, Arsenal were outstanding in the first half. Again, though, they reached the interval with only one goal to show for their efforts.
Dortmund, like Newcastle, came out with renewed belief, and a lot more intensity. Even before Beier's equaliser, the same player had missed a glorious chance when he failed to connect with a Joey Veerman cross. Arsenal were suddenly on the back foot.
They regained control after Dortmund's leveller, albeit while avoiding a scare when Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside. But their attempts to break down the visitors were unsuccessful. Good positions were wasted. They should have been out of sight.
Arteta couldn't believe it when the otherwise impressive Gyokeres skewed his header wide from Odegaard's cross. The Arsenal boss was on his knees when Timber's cut-back ricocheted off the post.
It is positive that they are creating so many chances. Their performance featured another bright showing from Noni Madueke. But they will need to find some cutting edge against City.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta : "I think it was a brilliant performance.
"The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today, is something to be very, very pleased about.
"There is very little more that you can demand from the team.
"But obviously there is the feeling that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance, with the amount of chances and situations.
"There is an element of luck and there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist, because I think what the team has done and shown today is the right direction.
"I love the way the team played. I think there's no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were, how connected everybody was to the game. It was great to watch.
"It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball hasn't ended up in the back of the net. That's my feeling."
Borussia Dortmund boss Niko Kovac : "I thought VAR should have looked at the handball. It would have been worth a check.
"They are trying to intervene less, but it doesn't mean you should not intervene when you should do.
"In such a situation, you have to at least have someone in the VAR room saying, 'Let's just look at it.'
"I am not crying about it. It is what it is. We got a point. It is a big point away to Arsenal, a big one for all of us, our fans, our team, and the club."

İsviçre'nin Lozan kentinde mahkeme, Senegal Futbol Federasyonu'nun (FSF), Afrika Futbol Konfederasyonu (CAF) Temyiz Kurulu kararına yaptığı itirazı kabul etti. Kurul, Senegal'in Fas'ta oynanan final maçını hükmen kaybettiğine karar vermiş ve ev sahibi Fas'ı 3-0 galip ilan etmişti. Böylece Senegal'in sahada kazandığı 1-0'lık sonuç yeniden geçerli oldu.
Mart ayında CAF, çok sayıda Senegalli futbolcunun penaltı kararını protesto ederek sahayı terk etmesinin ardından Fas'ı 3-0 galip ilan etmiş ve şampiyonluğu Fas'a vermişti.
Fas Futbol Federasyonu, Senegal takımının geçici olarak sahadan ayrılarak turnuva kurallarını ihlal ettiğini savunmuştu. Federasyon ayrıca hakem Jean-Jacques Ngambo Ndala'nın maçı erken bitirmesi gerektiğini ileri sürmüştü. Ancak hakem, karşılaşmayı 109'uncu dakikada yeniden başlatmıştı.
CAS heyeti bu değerlendirmeye katılmadı. Mahkeme, "Hakem oyunu yeniden başlatmak için düdüğünü çaldığında, maçın devam etmesi için gerekli koşulların yerine geldiğini değerlendirmişti. Her iki takım da yeniden sahadaydı ve karşılaşmaya devam etmeye istekli olduklarını belirtmişti," açıklamasını yaptı.
Mahkeme heyetine göre hakemin kararının etkileri yalnızca saha içiyle sınırlıydı. Bu nedenle karar, "saha içi kararları" doktrini kapsamında değerlendirildi.
Bu doktrin uyarınca CAS, kurallar keyfi veya kötü niyetli biçimde uygulanmadığı sürece hakemlerin saha içindeki kararlarını yeniden incelemiyor.
CAS, "Heyet, hakemin son derece gergin bir ortamda karar vermek zorunda kaldığını kabul etti. Ancak bu koşullar, kararın 'keyfi' olarak nitelendirilmesini haklı çıkarmıyor," ifadelerini kullandı.
Üç üyeden oluşan CAS heyetinin kararı oy birliğiyle aldığı belirtildi.
Senegal Futbol Federasyonu, teknik direktör Pape Thiaw ve bazı futbolcular ise CAF'ın ayrı disiplin süreçleri kapsamında daha önce yaptırımlara maruz kalmıştı.

Gunmen seized dozens of hostages at a supermarket in the Colombian tourist city of Cartagena on Tuesday, triggering a tense, hours-long standoff with police, troops and special forces who surrounded the building and cut power to the area.
Authorities said the gunmen had attempted to rob an armored vehicle before fleeing into the supermarket and taking about 30 people hostage as police closed in.
By nightfall, 10 hostages had been released, police told AFP, five of them elderly women.
Reuters images showed heavily ⁠armed military and police gathered outside the supermarket.
Colombia 's president arrived at the scene of the standoff in Cartagena. Police and AFP reporters on the scene said Abelardo de la Espriella 's motorcade had arrived in the area – where he will ostensibly take control of a massive operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.
"Thirty people were kidnapped, five of ​whom have already been released. They are ‌older women," De la Espriella had said earlier from the city of Villavicencio, where he traveled following an overnight ‌bombing there.
"All the capabilities of our various security forces, ​have now been deployed, including special units," he added.

(From left) Moyin Odeniran, Mo Mahir and Tom Whittaker all made Tuesday night's final
Spoiler warning: This story reveals details of The Great British Bake Off final
Moyin Odeniran said he was "in shock" after being crowned the winner of the 17th series of The Great British Bake Off.
The 22-year-old from Loughton, Essex, described it as a "very busy time" as he juggled competing in the Channel 4 baking competition with completing his university studies .
Despite his dissertation being due a month after filming wrapped, Odeniran achieved a first in his political economy degree at King's College London.
He beat fellow finalists Tom Whittaker, from West Yorkshire, and Birmingham student Mo Mahir to the title in Tuesday night's episode.
"I don't know how that happened, I don't know how I got here. I can't believe it – I am in shock," the talented baker said.
"I have made friends for life and I have just loved every single second of it, and I don't think I could have asked for anything more."
Judge Paul Hollywood described Odeniran's efforts as "pure magic" after watching his jubilant celebrations with family and friends.
"He has done an amazing job because out of all the bakers he struggled at the beginning, and he actually got better and better," Hollywood said.
Fellow judge Nigella Lawson praised Odeniran as a "worthy winner", but also said the other finalists were "sensational".
The high-stakes final saw the three contestants tasked with making a citrus celebration cake, creme brulee donuts and a "spectacular tribute to iconic British landscapes".
Reflecting on his performance in the final, Odeniran said: "I didn't want to put too much pressure on myself, but I knew I had put my best foot forward.
"I couldn't have done anything better than I did and I had a great time doing it."
He said he got "quite exhausted" while filming the series and praised his mother, sister and close friends for their support.
"Earlier on, some of the challenges were quite difficult for me and I was shocked that I kept going through," Odeniran said.
"Before you get there you think you know how to bake, and by week two you question whether you know anything about baking."
He shared his gratitude at being able to learn from Lawson and Hollywood.
"I will never forget my time there and the friendships made which will always continue," the winner added.
Prior to the final, Odeniran told BBC Essex he planned to view it at a huge "watch party" at his local church .

Ay, 24 Kasım Salı akşamı 17.53'te İkizler burcunda dolunay evresine giriyor ve Ocak'tan bu yana ilk süper ay olarak gökyüzünde daha büyük, daha parlak görünüyor. İletişim, merak ve ikilik temalarını öne çıkaran bu dolunaya Uranüs eşlik ediyor; bu da beklenmedik haberler ve ani fikir değişiklikleri anlamına geliyor. Dolunayın her burçta dokunduğu alana göre bu geceye yakışan 12 film belli oldu.
Ay, 24 Kasım Salı akşamı Dünya'ya en yakın noktalarından birinde dolunay evresine giriyor ve normalden daha büyük, daha parlak görünüyor. Astrolojide İkizler; iletişim, merak, kelimeler ve ikilik demek. Güneş'in Yay'da, Ay'ın karşısında İkizler'de olduğu bu gecede söylenmemiş sözler gün yüzüne çıkıyor.
Uranüs'ün eşlik etmesi ise beklenmedik haberlere ve ani fikir değişikliklerine işaret ediyor. Dolunayın her burçta dokunduğu alana göre seçilen filmler şöyle:
İkizler dolunayı Koç burcunun iletişim, yakın çevre ve kısa yolculuklar alanını aydınlatıyor. Ertelediğin bir konuşma bu günlerde kendiliğinden gündeme gelebilir.
Richard Linklater'ın 1995 yapımı Gün Doğmadan (Before Sunrise), Viyana'da tanışan iki yabancının sabaha kadar süren sohbetini anlatıyor. Ethan Hawke ve Julie Delpy'nin filmi, tek bir konuşmanın bir hayatı nasıl değiştirebileceğini gösteriyor.
Dolunay Boğa'nın para ve kaynaklar alanında. Kazancını, harcamalarını ve kendine biçtiğin değeri yeniden düşünebilirsin.
Bong Joon-ho'nun Oscar'da En İyi Film ödülünü kazanan ilk İngilizce olmayan yapım olarak tarihe geçen Parazit, yoksul bir ailenin zengin bir ailenin hayatına sızışını anlatırken para ile değer arasındaki çizgiyi sorgulatıyor.
Dolunay doğrudan senin burcunda ve Uranüs de hemen yanında. Kimliğin, imajın ve kendini nasıl gördüğün konusunda ani bir aydınlanma yaşayabilirsin.
7 Oscar kazanan Her Şey Her Yerde Aynı Anda, çoklu evrenlerde kendi farklı versiyonlarıyla karşılaşan Evelyn'in hikayesini anlatıyor. Michelle Yeoh'nun başrolündeki film , İkizler'in ikilik temasına bu kadar uyan nadir yapımlardan.
Yengeç için dolunay bilinçaltı ve geride bırakılması gerekenler alanında gerçekleşiyor. Kafanda dönüp duran bir anıyı ya da ilişkiyi kapatma zamanı gelmiş olabilir.
Jim Carrey ve Kate Winslet'in başrolündeki 2004 yapımı Sil Baştan, ayrıldığı sevgilisini hafızasından sildirmeye karar veren bir adamı anlatıyor. Peki unutmak gerçekten iyileştirir mi?
Dolunay Aslan'ın arkadaşlıklar, topluluklar ve gelecek hayalleri alanında. Hayatındaki insanların sana ne kattığını daha net göreceksin.
Gerçek bir hikayeden uyarlanan Can Dostum, felçli zengin bir adamla ona bakıcılık yapmaya başlayan genç Driss arasındaki beklenmedik dostluğu anlatıyor. François Cluzet ve Omar Sy'nin uyumu hâlâ hafızalarda.
Başak burcu için dolunay kariyer ve toplumdaki konum alanında. İş hayatında bir sonuç alabilir ya da yön değiştirmeye karar verebilirsin.
Meryl Streep ve Anne Hathaway'li Şeytan Marka Giyer, hırs ile kendin olmak arasında kalan Andy'nin hikayesi. Üstelik filmin devamı bu yıl 1 Mayıs'ta vizyona girdi; ikisini art arda izlemek için daha iyi bir gece yok.
Dolunay Terazi'nin yolculuklar, eğitim ve yeni bakış açıları alanında. İçindeki kaçma isteği bu günlerde iyice yüksek sesle konuşabilir.
Ben Stiller'ın yönetip başrolünü üstlendiği Walter Mitty'nin Gizli Yaşamı, hayallerinde yaşayan bir arşiv çalışanının İzlanda'ya uzanan gerçek bir maceraya atılmasını anlatıyor.
Akrep burcu için dolunay sırlar, ortak paralar ve derin bağlar alanında gerçekleşiyor. Bir ilişkide perde arkasında kalan bir gerçek ortaya çıkabilir.
David Fincher'ın 2014 yapımı Kayıp Kız, evlilik yıldönümünde ortadan kaybolan Amy ile şüphelerin odağındaki kocası Nick'i anlatıyor. Rosamund Pike'ın performansı Oscar adaylığı getirmişti.
Güneş senin burcunda, dolunay ise tam karşında, yani ilişkiler ve ortaklıklar alanında. Partnerinle ya da yakın bir dostunla ilişkiyi tanımlayan bir konuşma yapabilirsin.
Senaryosu Nora Ephron'a ait Harry Sally ile Tanışınca, 'Kadınla erkek arkadaş olabilir mi?' sorusunu yıllara yayılan sohbetlerle tartışıyor. Billy Crystal ve Meg Ryan'ın filmi tam bir kış klasiği.
Oğlak için dolunay günlük düzen, sağlık ve iş alışkanlıkları alanında. Neyin seni yorduğunu, neyin iyi geldiğini ayırt etmenin tam zamanı.
Wim Wenders'ın Perfect Days (Mükemmel Günler) filmi, Tokyo'da tuvalet temizleyen Hirayama'nın sade ama dolu dolu günlerini izliyor. Kōji Yakusho bu rolle Cannes'da En İyi Erkek Oyuncu ödülünü kazanmıştı.
Dolunay Kova'nın aşk, yaratıcılık ve keyif alanını aydınlatıyor. Bir tutku ya da heyecan verici bir flört gündemine girebilir.
Damien Chazelle'in 6 Oscar kazanan La La Land filmi, Los Angeles'ta hayallerinin peşindeki bir caz piyanisti ile oyuncu adayının aşkını anlatıyor. Ryan Gosling ve Emma Stone'un filmi, hayaller ile aşk arasındaki seçimi sorgulatıyor.
Balık burcu için dolunay ev, aile ve kökler alanında gerçekleşiyor. Ailenle ilgili bir mesele çözülebilir ya da geçmişe dair bir duygu yeniden canlanabilir.
Çağan Irmak'ın 2005 yapımı Babam ve Oğlum, yıllar sonra oğluyla köyüne dönen Sadık ile babası Hüseyin Efendi'nin hikayesini anlatıyor. Çetin Tekindor ve Fikret Kuşkan'ın filmi, izleyenlerin gözyaşlarını tutamadığı yapımların başında geliyor.

Sarı-kırmızılı taraftarlar mücadele öncesi açtıkları pankartlarla ve yaptıkları tezahüratlarla Filistin'e destek oldu.

Galatasaray Başkanı Dursun Özbek, dev mücadele öncesi HT Spor'a yaptığı açıklamada İsrai'in sarı-kırmızılı taraftarları UEFA'ya şikayet ettiğini açıkladı.

“Duyduk ki Netanyahu hükümeti, taraftarımızın Filistin halkına destek amacıyla açtığı pankartlar nedeniyle kulübümüzü UEFA’ya şikâyet etmiş.

Dünyanın dört bir yanında Filistin halkının maruz kaldığı zulme karşı yükselen ortak vicdani sesin de gösterdiği gibi bu, siyasi değil, insani ve vicdani bir duruştur.

Bu gelişmeler sonrası UEFA'dan da skandal bir tutum geldi. UEFA pankart konusunda Galatasaray 'a adeta aba altından sopa göstererek Filistin pankartlarının bir daha statta açılmamasını istedi.

İstanbul Anadolu Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından Şile Belediyesi ’ne yönelik yürütülen "suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurma", "irtikap", "rüşvet" ve "ihaleye fesat karıştırma" soruşturması kapsamında, 10 Temmuz 2025’te Belediye Başkanı Özgür Kabadayı’nın da aralarında bulunduğu şüpheliler gözaltına alınmış, Kabadayı tutuklanmıştı. Soruşturma kapsamında 23 Aralık’ta düzenlenen eş zamanlı operasyonda gözaltına alınan 22 şüpheliden 15’i tutuklanmış, soruşturmanın üçüncü dalga operasyonu ise 26 Haziran 2026’da gerçekleştirilmişti. Hazırlanan iddianamede, Kabadayı hakkında "icbar suretiyle irtikap", "resmi belgede sahtecilik", "dolandırıcılık", "rüşvet almak" ve "suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurma" suçları başta olmak üzere çeşitli suçlardan 33 yıl 3 aydan 92 yıla kadar hapis cezası talep edildi. İddianamede ayrıca, örgüt elebaşısı olduğu belirtilen Kabadayı’nın gerçekleştirilen eylemler nedeniyle ayrı ayrı cezalandırılması istendi. Anadolu 27. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’nde 10. celsesi görülen duruşma yoğunluk sebebiyle konferans salonunda gerçekleşti.
Duruşmaya, tutuklu sanık eski belediye başkanı Özgür Kabadayı ile Berkant Acil’inde aralarında bulunduğu 11 sanık ile bazı tutuksuz sanıklar katıldı. Salonda taraf avukatları da hazır bulundu. Şile Bezi Festivali'nde sahne alan sanatçı Sıla Gençoğlu Ses ve Görüntü Bilişim Sistemleri (SEGBİS) ile duruşmaya tanık olarak bağlandı.
Tanık olarak dinlenen şarkıcı Sıla Gençoğlu, "Ağırlıklı olarak 90 dakika sahne alır sonra oradan ayrılırız başka bir bilgim yok. Yetki belgesi, organizasyon firma üzerinden gelir. Menajer tarafından imza atarız. Vekaletim varsa menajerim de imzayı adıma atabilir ama genelde imzayı biz atıyoruz. Anlaşma organizasyon firma ile menajer üzerinden olur. O zamanki menajerim İsmail Serkan Güner ama şu anda kendisiyle çalışmıyorum. Bana gönderilen ücreti hatırlamıyorum. Ortalama konser ücretim hakkında net bir rakam söyleyemem bu işler benim üzerimden değil menajer üzerinden yürüyor. Para genelde benim hesabıma ya da şahıs şirket hesabıma yatar. Genelde belediye konseri veriyordum bu konudan sonra belediyelerle çalışmama kararı aldım. 2024 yılı yazında 625 bin lira ücretle ilgili bir bilgim yok hatırlamıyorum. Ben parayla ilgilenmiyorum sanatımla ilgileniyorum. Konser hizmetini verdiğimde sorunsuz ödeme yapıldı diye düşünüyorum. Bana yansıyan bir sorun olmadı. Bu işin bize Koşan Adam’dan geldiğini hatırlıyorum" şeklinde konuştu.
Babazula grubu üyesi Tanık Ümit Adakale, "Babazula grubunda çalışan bir elemanım. Bu konularla bir bağlantım yok. Organizasyona bizi Arif Sevik yönlendirdi. Müzisyen olarak WhatsApp grubumuz var, orada bilgi geldi. Grubumuzun aldığı ücret 20-25 bin liraydı. Ortalama ücretimiz bu şekildeydi parayı kişi başı aldık. Yaklaşık 45 dakika sürdü konserimiz. Konser ücreti konser yerinde zarf içinde nakit olarak ödendi" dedi.
Festivalde şarkıcı olarak sahne alan tanık Sena Şener, "Şile Bezi Festivali'nde müzisyen olarak görev aldım. Solo şarkıcı olarak sahneye çıkıyorum. Festivalde 1 gün bulundum. Festival süresi boyunca Zirve Müzik ile çalışıyordum. Zirve Müzik bana bu işi getirdi o şekilde dahil oldum. Hizmet karşılığında 50 bin lira anlaşma yaptık. Yetki belgesini imzalayıp imzalamadığımı hatırlamıyorum ama imza benim imzama benziyor. Ben o zaman sadece menajerimle muhatap oldum. Ücret Zirve Müzik tarafından hesabıma gönderildi" ifadelerini kullandı.

Dağılan yuvalarda eğer çocuk varsa boşanan eşler bir şekilde ömür boyu birbirleriyle görüşmek durumunda kalıyor elbette.
Ama bizim anlatacağımız olayın kahramanları olan eski çiftin birbirinin hayatından çıkmamasının tek sebebi çocukları değil, para! KOCASINA YARIM MİLYON DOLAR ÖDEMEK ZORUNDA Güzel oyuncu Jessica Alba ile Cash Warren, 16 yıl süren üç çocuklu evliliklerini geçen yıl bitirdi.
Hatta 45 yaşındaki Alba, Danny Ramirez ile yeni bir ilişkiye başladı. Ama evlilik resmen bitse de eski kocası Cash Warren ile aralarındaki "para" bağlantısı bitmedi.
Jessica Alba'nın, Cash Warren ile yaptığı boşanma anlaşması gereği ona yarım milyon dolardan fazla bir ödeme yapmasına mahkeme tarafından karar verildi.
Page Six tarafından ele geçirilen boşanma belgelerine göre Alba, eski kocası Warren'a 577 bir 481 dolar para ödeyecek.
Bu ödeme de Jessica Alba'nın şirketi HonorBar Inc'in kâr paylaşım planı kapsamındaki emeklilik haklarından yapılacak.
Ama bu kadar değil... Söz konusu tutar, Alba'nın şirketinin, ödemenin yapılacağı tarihe kadar yaşayacağı kazanç ya da kayıplara göre artıp azalabilecek.
Yani Alba'nın şirketi daha fazla kar elde ederse eski kocasına ödeyeceği miktar da artabilecek.
ALBA ESKİ KOCASINDAN DAHA ZENGİN Bu karar; eski çiftin bu yılın şubat ayıhda görülen boşanma davası sırasında yapılan anlaşmayla ilgili. Buna göre Alba eski kocasına 3 milyon doyar bir ödeme yapacaktı. Bunun da 1.5 milyon dolarlık iki taksit halinde yapılması karara bağlandı.
Bir not düşelim... Jessica Alba'nın kurucusu olduğu Honest Company'e 623 milyon dolar, eski kocası Cash Warren 'ın sahip olduğu çorap ve iç giyim firması Pair of Thieves'e 100 milyon değer biçildi. Ancak eski çift, 2008 yılında hayatlarını birleştirirken bir evlilik sözleşmesi imzalamadığı için Alba şimdi eski kocasına ödeme yapmak zorunda kaldı.
Bu arada eski çiftin boşanmasından kısa süre önce konuşulanlara bakılırsa, evliliklerinin özellikle son yıllarında eve para getiren kişi hep Jessica Alba oldu.
Hatta aralarındaki aşkın bittiğinden, çocuklar doğduktan sonra aynı evi paylaşan iki arkadaş gibi olduklarından dert yanan kişi de Jessica Alba olmuştu.
Eski çiftin 18 yaşında Honor, 15 yaşında Haven ve 8 yaşında Hayes adında üç çocuğu bulunuyor. Alba ile Warren çocuklarının ortak velayetine sahip.

Late-night hosts discussed disgraced Nvidia CEO’s quick return to his role after pressure from shareholder Trump
Late-night hosts reacted to the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia under political pressure from Donald Trump .
“Who doesn’t love a good comeback story?” said Jimmy Kimmel on Monday evening, just a day after the board of Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang under pressure from Donald Trump to reinstall his friend as head of the trillion-dollar computer chip company. Huang was ousted just two weeks ago after it was revealed that he had multiple affairs , including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with Nvidia subordinates.
“After 10 grueling days of forced unemployment, the board at Nvidia today voted to reinstate their former CEO, who, according to our president , did nothing wrong ,” Kimmel explained. “All this guy did was cheat on his wife with two employees and a Chinese spy. Who hasn’t done that?”
The reinstatement included an assurance from the Nvidia board that they have “every confidence” in Huang to lead the company. “Which, of course, had nothing to do with the pressure they got from our Silicon man-in-chief, who has at least 62m reasons why he wanted his pal in charge,” said Kimmel, referring to Trump’s $62m reported Nvidia stock worth. “After the board made it clear that they were unequivocally moving on, Trump called them personally to harangue them. And if you think that sounds fishy, it’s not. It’s called being a good friend.”
“There’s nothing unusual about a president who owns a huge amount of stock in a company putting his little carrot thumb on the scale in a way that immediately boosts that company’s stock price,” Kimmel mocked. “I’m sure it also didn’t hurt that Huang donated $25m to the big, stupid ballroom he’s building.”
“And you think he would be ashamed of this! Not at all.” Trump wrote on Truth Social that the Nvidia board “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO” and that the US government has “no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security”.
“Says the man who stashed classified documents in the toilet at his country club,” Kimmel quipped.
“And if all this insanity wasn’t enough,” Trump went on to post an AI-doctored photo of his own 2024 assassination attempt, with Huang holding up a red bra. “What a profoundly stupid time to be alive,” said Kimmel.
And on Late Night, Seth Meyers also responded to the latest development in the Nvidia saga. “So Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and his company possibly broke the law and allowed China to get its hand on their highly sought-after computer chips,” he said. “And yet, throughout all of that, the president’s main concern was empathy – not for American workers impacted by AI, but for his good friend Jensen.”
Speaking to reporters this weekend, Trump claimed that he asked Huang, “Did you have any idea she was a spy? And he said: ‘I had no idea that she was a spy.’”
“Yeah, that’s how spying works!” Meyers laughed. “They don’t wear shirts that say ‘ask me about being a spy.’”
“Trump is supposed to be the America first guy, the guy who says only he can take on China,” he continued. “Why would he excuse potentially illegal behavior of a tech CEO who might have harmed America's national security? Is there some other possible explanation here? And does it perhaps involve lots of money? Not for us, but for him.” Meyers then played several news clips reporting on Trump’s $62m in Nvidia stock, as well as the company’s ties to businesses run by his son Donald Trump Jr.
“Tech oligarchs consider us expendable,” Meyers concluded. “We can be replaced by AI. But the second they lose a job or face consequences for their actions, Trump will swoop in and save them.”

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card shown to him at Anfield overturned by the Football Association - even though referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.
Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into Sunday's match.
Isak had run onto a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought down the Swede.
New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at a decision he felt had changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.
"The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.
"But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul."
The FA backed that view, meaning Yoro will be clear to face Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Saturday.
However, in the latest edition of Mic'd Up on Sky Sports, Webb said Barrott got it right.
"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," he said.
'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?
How on earth can the head of referees say a decision was right, but the FA say it was wrong?
"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable," Webb said. "Certainly not clearly wrong."
Not clearly and obviously wrong for a VAR intervention, but clearly and obviously wrong for the FA to rescind the red card.
You wonder how the general fan is supposed to understand it all.
The FA's appeals process is notoriously difficult to predict, especially on highly borderline situations like Yoro.
A commission features three people, usually former players though sometimes there is a retired official is on the panel.
A simple majority is needed, so a club just needs two people to agree with them.
It's why clubs might appeal against red cards when it seems impossible to win, you just never know.
Such was the split of opinion on Yoro, United always stood a chance of at least getting those key two votes.
And this is the crux of appeals process. An FA commission is just the subjective opinion of three people.
Do the appeal again tomorrow with three different panel members, and United might lose.
This is why Pro Ref don't use the outcome of FA appeals to determine how games are officiated.
Two years ago, Brentford's Christian Norgaard won an appeal against a red card at Everton. That was a split 2:1 vote, but enough to say a decision was wrong.
Pro Ref told its referees not to alter their interpretation based on this vote.
Let's throw in another one. The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel.
Earlier this season, Brighton appealed against Pascal Struijk's VAR red card at Sunderland.
An FA commission upheld the appeal, but in contradiction the KMI Panel voted the VAR intervention was correct.
This will forever be the problem with officiating, and indeed any hope of true consistency with VAR.
Was Yoro's red card right or wrong? On which side of the fence will the KMI Panel fall?
Football is just a floating mass of subjectivity. Of referees, of VARs, of panel members and of fans. It just depends whose opinion you ask.
Sporting coach Paulo Fonseca speaks to the media ahead of the Champions League clash with Manchester United
United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT).
The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break.
But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile".
"I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon.
"Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma.
"Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day."
United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions.
Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect.
"Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said.
"I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict."

Mauricio Pochettino has criticised officiating in English football, saying: “We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be in the level to drive [it],” after Leny Yoro’s Anfield red card was overturned on Tuesday.
Despite the Football Association ruling the Frenchman’s early sending-off in Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool was “wrongful dismissal”, Manchester United remain furious at the decision, and at Pro Ref, the elite officials’ organisation.
Dominik Szoboszlai scored the subsequent free-kick which put Liverpool on the road to victory, and United were dismayed by Howard Webb , the Pro Ref chief, saying he could understand why Sam Barrott gave the red card and the video assistant referees backed the decision.
United remain insistent that Alexander Isak would not have reached the ball before their goalkeeper, Senne Lammens, as he was brought down by Yoro and they argue this can be objectively proved. The club also believe there was an error of process as the recording of the video officials shows a quick look at the incident with no due consideration and they have confirmed they will raise this with the Premier League and Pro Ref.
When asked about this, Pochettino also claimed Szoboszlai’s strike should not have stood as Bradley Barcola touched United’s wall. The head coach said: “We didn’t pay attention, but Bruno [Fernandes] was aware: no one talked about that the goal wasn’t legal. Should disallow the goal because Barcola was touching our wall, and maybe in the last two years maybe they changed the rule. Very disappointed because I think this type of thing never can happen.
“My question always was the same: OK, we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship [the heat of moment] within the game.
“But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Because now, are we going to repeat the game? We need to take the time to review the situation. We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We need to drive in the best way.
“We love the technology, yes? We accept that the technology is there, yes? [So] what are they doing?”
Pochettino also referenced Erling Haaland’s winner in Manchester City’s 1-0 win at United in September. Pro Ref later admitted it should not have been allowed after the video assistant referee ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the buildup.
“It’s not only this mistake or the mistake against Haaland in Manchester City when I was a spectator. It’s how after it affects everything. I need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce and to say, yes, we were right, or the decision wasn’t good. And now, where are the three points? It’s a thing that we need to think a little bit more deep.”
Speaking before the card was rescinded, Webb said: “Isak’s got control of the ball, knocks it past Yoro. He’s moving at pace and a foul comes and knocks him down. There’s a question mark around whether or not he would get on to that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. The VAR checks to see whether that decision was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion it wasn’t.
“Most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but it’s debatable. [It’s] certainly not clearly wrong.”
The Liverpool defeat came in Pochettino’s first match as the United head coach. His side are next at Sporting in Wednesday’s fifth Champions League group game, having suffered a 4-1 humiliation at Como in the previous one under Michael Carrick. Despite this and Sunday’s reverse, which left United second-bottom in the Premier League, Pochettino was bullish when asked about the comments of Paulo Fonseca, the Sporting coach, who dismissed any notion that the visitors are fragile.
He said: “What I found is that people [outside] want it to look like we’re fragile. I don’t say that we are fragile. We are strong, we have great mentality. There are things we need to improve, of course, many things that we need to improve, but it’s normal when you are in a position that we are in the Premier League.

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro (second left) is shown a red card by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.
Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.
United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.
Pochettino said he had some sympathy with referee Sam Barrott but he is livid at how the situation played out.
"I am very disappointed," the Argentine said. "This type of thing can never happen.
"We can accept the referee can make a mistake. But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play 11 by 11? No.
"We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We accept that the technology is there but what are they doing?"
United are furious at both the nature of the audio of the incident, and referees' chief Howard Webb defending referee Barrott's decision and the VAR John Brooks' reinforcing it on the Mic'd Up programme, which was shown on Sky Sports.
They intend to take the matter up with both the Premier League and ProRef.
It is the second time this season United been on the wrong end of a major VAR error.
'And the three points?' - Pochettino after Yoro red overturned
Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby at Old Trafford on 13 September was allowed to stand even though a clearly offside Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play.
Instead, he has doubled down on the call, saying: "I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball."
The club are unhappy at the speed the on-field decision was confirmed. It is thought United used data around Isak's top speed and his chances of reaching the ball in their defence of Yoro to the FA. They claim this could have been done "within minutes" of the incident occurring.
This is not the only bone of contention at Old Trafford around the incident.
Pochettino also pointed out Liverpool forward Bradley Barcola was too close to the United wall from the resulting free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal should have been disallowed.
"No-one talked about [the fact] that the goal wasn't legal," said Pochettino. "Barcola was touching our wall. It must be disallowed.
"We need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce it and to say, the decision wasn't good. And now, the three points, where are the three points?"
What referee's chief Webb said about the incident on the Mic'd Up programme.
"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.
"That was the referee's call made on the field, and then the VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn't.
"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. and
"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.
"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable. Certainly not clearly wrong."
United's fury over Yoro and the way the situation has been handled cannot completely obscure the fact they lost 4-0 in Pochettino's first game in charge.
It extended a terrible start to the season that has seen the Red Devils win on just three occasions - and only once in the Premier League, against newly-promoted Ipswich in August.
The club are 19th in the Premier League and facing up to the possibility of being relegated for the first time since 1973-74.
Yet Pochettino is adamant there is no fragility about his new squad.
"The situation is fragile in [terms of] the environment, or the people want it to look like we're fragile. But I don't say that we are fragile. I think we are strong.
"There are many things we need to improve. It's normal to be in a different position, and everyone can use different words to describe the situation.
"But we are a strong team. They showed that last season, capable of finishing third. I think we are going to turn around the situation and start to perform in the level like before Bruno [Fernandes] said, deserve to be at this club."
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino (left) and skipper Bruno Fernandes speak to the media ahead of the Champions League clash with Sporting in Lisbon
Skipper Bruno Fernandes revealed at the weekend talks over a new United contract were on hold.
The 32-year-old's present deal expires in the summer, although the club have an option to extend it by 12 months.
Speaking alongside Pochettino at a media conference before his first meeting with Sporting since he left to join United in a £47m deal in January 2020, Fernandes said his sole focus at present is to drag United out of the mire.
"For us to start winning games, then we can start speaking about contract," he said.
"It's not important now. It's irrelevant. Obviously, I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look into that way because I haven't got much left in my contract, but I'm not really worried about that.
"I'm more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back in a position that we can be proud of, and we're not there at the moment."

Wirtz moved from Bayer Leverkusen to Liverpool for £116m in 2025
Florian Wirtz says he is enjoying his best form yet at Liverpool and benefiting from Andoni Iraola's confidence and Jurgen Klopp's advice.
Wirtz, 23, scored in Liverpool's 4-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday and has three goals and six assists this season.
The Germany midfielder made the £116m move from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025 and after failing to make his mark in his first campaign in England, is beginning to showcase his quality for Iraola's side.
Speaking in Belgium before Liverpool 's Champions League game against Club Brugge, Wirtz said: "I can't really say that I've changed that much.
"I've become a bit better on a physical level and that's the only reason that could explain it."
He also said he has been picking the brains of Germany manager Klopp, the former Liverpool boss, while on international duty.
"He tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here and tries to give me some advice to get successful over here as he has shown how it is done," Wirtz said.
"He can give me some good advice. It's always small things. More private things.
"But he is speaking good about the club, the region, the people, and that helps to hear someone who has experienced it for a long time."
On the influence of Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot as Liverpool head coach in the summer, Wirtz added: "He is bringing me back in a place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football, and I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I'm really happy about that.
Liverpool have nine points from their four Champions League games, having won their first three before losing to Fenerbahce in Istanbul this month.
Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch are both absent from the travelling squad with injuries, with Iraola confirming that Gakpo will be out for the Merseyside derby this weekend, while adding that it is "difficult to say" for Gravenberch.

France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering. The new charges are related to the Sarkozy couple's actions during the case examining illegal campaign funding from Libyan strongman Muammar Gaddafi over which Sarkozy was imprisoned last year.
France 's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy , his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy , and a paparazzi boss will stand trial next year over alleged witness tampering in a case over funding for his 2007 election, a source close to the case said Tuesday.
France's right-wing leader from 2007 to 2012 has been embroiled in legal woes since leaving office.
Last year he became modern France's first former president to go to jail over seeking illegal campaign funding from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi in exchange for help restoring his international image.
Read more Ex-president Sarkozy’s 20-day prison diary: ‘Like the Count of Monte Cristo’?
The former head of state was freed from jail after 20 days pending his appeal, and an appeals court is to issue its ruling on Monday.
One of the main accusers in the case was French-Lebanese businessman Ziad Takieddine , who died in Lebanon last year.
In 2016 he claimed he helped deliver up to €5 million ($6 million) in cash from Gaddafi to Sarkozy and the former president's chief of staff in 2006 and 2007.
But in November 2020, Takieddine suddenly retracted his incriminating statement in an interview with French media.
Read more Key Lebanese-French accuser in Sarkozy Libya funding probe dies on eve of verdict
This prompted accusations that Sarkozy and his wife enlisted the help of paparazzi queen Mimi Marchand to pay the witness to change his mind, something they have always denied.
Bruni is suspected of having requested a clandestine phone line in late 2019 to communicate with Marchand about the Takieddine operation.
A court will in November next year try Sarkozy and Bruni on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering, the source told AFP.
Marchand stands accused of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as witness tampering.
Their lawyers did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.
The defendants face a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison and a fine of €150,000.
Sarkozy has received two definitive convictions in other cases – linked to overspending in his failed 2012 re-election bid, and later trying to extract favours from a judge.
Marchand was last year handed an 18-month suspended prison sentence for blackmailing a television host, who feared the paparazzi boss would publish images of her daughter leaving police custody.

Rangers scored three goals in 11 minutes at the start of the second half after a triple substitution
Rangers manager Derek McInnes says his team's naivety and complacency made their task more difficult in their thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen, but hailed their ability to get the job done.
The Ibrox outfit had to navigate a tense finale as they held off a defiant Aberdeen side, just three days after their dramatic late win at Motherwell , and are now just a point behind Celtic at the Scottish Premiership summit.
Rangers had roared into a 3-1 lead after a stunning 11-minute burst at the start of the second half overwhelmed the visitors, who led at the break through Brad Lyons' header.
However, the Dons pulled one back through vibrant youngster Findlay Marshall and both sides had opportunities to add to the scoreline in a gripping closing passage.
"We put ourselves in the mire there, we were so naive at times," McInnes told Sky Sports.
"The biggest part for me is how we lose the initiative by just being too complacent and that has to change because we won't always outscore opponents.
"Once we got ourselves in front you think 'just keep the shoulder to the wheel'. We hit them like a train and they were 3-1 down because of the speed, intensity, intelligence and then we started to play backwards.
"We played more backwards passes than I can remember in a long time, we need to show more control."
Rangers beat Aberdeen in five-goal thriller to move within one of Celtic
McInnes' displeasure at the first-half display manifested itself in a half-time triple substitution as Findlay Curtis, Tuur Rommens and Kim Min-Su were hurled into the action.
Rangers were a different team in the 11 minutes that followed, with goals from Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin turning the game on its head and flipping the mood of the Ibrox faithful.
"For us it was all about winning, we've won the game and we'll dust ourselves down," McInnes added after a 14th straight game without defeat.
"It was three good goals and I'm delighted by the impact of the subs and we dug it out, but we made it harder for ourselves."
That ability to grind out wins was evident at Fir Park on Saturday and was apparent again at Ibrox. Belief is growing among Rangers supporters, who are longing for a first league title in six years.
They have won six points from losing positions this season, a tally bettered only by St Johnstone and Celtic, who have seven apiece.
A win over Falkirk on Saturday, before Celtic travel to face Hearts on Sunday, would put Rangers top of the table for just the second time this season.
For the umpteenth time this season, Rangers were indebted to in-form striker Naderi.
The 23-year-old struggled for a consistent run of games in the early stages of his Ibrox career, but has more shown his worth with Youssef Chermiti and Lawrence Shankland sidelined through injury.
He has 13 goal contributions in 13 league appearances - eight goals and five assists - and also fired Rangers into the Premier Sports Cup final with his winner against Aberdeen at Hampden earlier this month.
"A lot of players have had plaudits recently, but where would Rangers be without Naderi?," former Rangers striker Kris Boyd asked on Sky Sports.
"He's scored big goals for Rangers this season. His goal return has been outstanding and they're big, big goals for Rangers."
Naderi, who featured twice for the Czech Republic during the international break, has the Scottish Premiership's highest expected goals (xG) and xG per 90 minutes.
His perfectly weighted assist for Gassama showed the touch of a player full of confidence and playing at the peak of his powers.
After weathering an early Rangers storm, Aberdeen took the lead and looked well worth their advantage at half-time.
For all of their endeavour and late surge, they failed to recover from their 11-minute capitulation. Still, Aberdeen legend Willie Miller was heartened by the performance under new head coach Mario Frick.
"It's been a long time since I've seen a performance as good as that from an Aberdeen side, albeit it was a defeat," Miller said.
"They pushed Rangers all the way. It will be a learning process for them, you'd certainly hope that would be the case."
15-year-old Andrew Fasanya's introduction shows Frick has no issues playing young players who merit game time, and 20-year-old Marshall was perhaps the standout performer of the night.
"When Aberdeen got their second, they gave as good as they got," McCall added.
"It's the type of game, and Aberdeen will be gutted to have lost it, but you can see progress, an idea, a bond with the supporters.
"A young Scottish player [Marshall], I thought was the best player on the park, too."

Bellingham has scored seven goals this season but this will be one to remember
Manager Jose Mourinho described Jude Bellingham as "without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world" following a wonder goal which inspired a brilliant second-half performance for Real Madrid in a 5-1 win against PSV .
Mourinho opted to leave the England midfielder out of the starting line-up for Tuesday's Champions League game at the Bernabeu - an understandable decision given the demands of Madrid's fixture schedule and the strength in depth at his disposal.
But after watching his side trail 1-0 at half-time against the Dutch side, Mourinho knew changes were needed.
"He is an amazing player that has everything," the Portuguese manager said. "He has physicality, he understands the game, he has absolutely everything. Today, he has changed how the game was evolving."
Captain Fede Valverde equalised in the 50th minute and 10 minutes later Bellingham produced his moment of magic.
Receiving the ball just outside the penalty area, he took two touches to lift it into position before unleashing a magnificent volley with the outside of his right footr, leaving PSV keeper Matej Kovar with no chance.
It was a sensational finish, executed with extraordinary precision.
"I was a bit surprised, honestly," Bellingham said about the goal. "I knew that I could control the ball well and get it into my grasp. But normally from there, I'm looking to see who's on as an option to play through.
"It popped up nicely and I thought I'm just going to hit it. So yeah, it was a nice goal and important for the team, being the second goal, and gave us control."
The 23-year-old celebrated in trademark fashion, standing with his arms outstretched in front of the home supporters as thousands serenaded him with chants of 'Hey Jude'.
It was his fourth goal in his past five appearances for Real.
Asked whether he should be compared to Real and France legend Zinedine Zidane, who won the Ballon d'Or and World Cup in 1998, Bellingham maintained his humility.
"I think Zidane is much better than me. He's much more elegant and he's my idol," he said.
'I'm just going to hit it!' - Bellingham reacts to stunning goal
Kylian Mbappe scored two more goals and Vinicius Junior put away the fifth to complete a super turnaround from a team that had looked short of ideas in the first half.
At the suggestion that he is currently in the form of his life, Bellingham said: "I think you're only as good as your next one [game]. Your last one doesn't really matter.
"But my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game. Thinking about my best form or being the best player in the world doesn't mean anything to me."
For Bellingham, the ability to respond when things are not going according to plan is what separates the best teams from the rest.
"We're managing to show that mentality that good teams do, that even if you're not playing well, you can raise the level at any point," he said.
His adaptation to life in Spain has also been an important part of that journey.
Asked about his increasingly impressive Spanish, Bellingham admitted he still gets nervous when speaking the language in public.
"It's getting a little bit better. I get a little bit nervous speaking to you guys. It's much easier in the changing room," he joked to journalists.
"I'm loving living in Spain. I'm loving the club. I think for English players it's such an important thing to go and move abroad and learn new things and I've obviously benefited massively from that."
And while his performances have inevitably brought renewed attention to individual awards, Bellingham said that personal recognition is not what motivates him.
Asked about the Ballon d'Or, he said his focus was only on the team.
"I don't care about the Ballon d'Or, honestly. I want to win a lot of titles with the team, the Champions League, the League."
"The Ballon d'Or is something for you, journalists, to vote and create a bit of tension. But for me it's more important that the team win."

Viktor Gyokeres has scored three goals in all competitions this season for Arsenal.
It might be emerging more as a theme than as a major problem, but in recent weeks Arsenal cannot seem to finish off matches when they are on top.
In their past nine outings across all competitions, just once have the Gunners won a game by more than a single goal.
The latest frustration came in Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, though perspective is needed. Arsenal might consider it as two points dropped having gone into half-time ahead, but they remain unbeaten in the current Champions League league phase and have not lost at this stage of the competition for more than two years.
But of late, despite dominating large parts of matches, Arsenal have had periods where they have dropped off and allowed opponents back into the game.
Against Slavia Prague away in the Champions League, after scoring twice in the first half, Arsenal 's standards dropped. The same happened against Newcastle in the Premier League last weekend where they found themselves 2-1 behind in the second half having led at the break, before recovering to eventually draw 2-2.
They are producing periods of high-level football, but the struggles to consistently turn that into more goals can lead to nervy finishes.
In the draw with Bundesliga leaders Dortmund, Arsenal had 30 shots but just four of those attempts were on target.
Boss Mikel Arteta mentioned the failure to capitalise post match, though was keen to praise his side's "brilliant performance".
"The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today and what we've done out there, is just something to be very, very pleased [about] because there is very little more that you can demand from the team," Arteta said.
"But obviously, the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance in the amount of chances (and) situations.
"There is an element of luck; there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist because I think what the team has done and shown today, I think it's the right direction."
Arteta made six changes to the side that drew with Newcastle , with one of the biggest calls to rest striker Kai Havertz and bring in Viktor Gyokeres.
The striker has had a difficult season so far, with four of his seven starts coming in the Champions League against opposition where Arsenal have been favourites.
However, Gyokeres scored a powerful effort from outside the area to give Arsenal the lead against Dortmund.
Overall though, it ended up being a mixed night for the 28-year-old as he missed a header from inside the six-yard-box that would have surely won the game for the Gunners late on.
Arteta was asked if the chances his side are missing were down to mentality, misfortune or composure.
"There is an element of luck here because how some of the goals they haven't gone inside, I don't know.
"The execution can be better, but everything that is in between that, I think it was really, really good."
Arteta was also full of praise for Gyokeres, with particular emphasis on the striker's link-up play; an element of his game at times criticised.
"What I love the most is how connected he was to the team," Arteta said.
"We used him many times in different ways. His link-up play, the way he held the ball, the way he threaded in behind and stretched the pitch.
"There was a lot to like in that performance and that's the Viktor that we needed."
Noni Madueke has been Arsenal 's best attacker in recent weeks.
The winger, who was left out of the last England squad, is enjoying a run in the Arsenal starting XI with Bukayo Saka out injured and is taking his opportunity.
Madueke has registered a goal and two assists in his past three games and was again the best Arsenal forward against Dortmund.
The Gunners host Manchester City on Sunday and are currently six points clear at the top of the Premier League table.
Madueke, who was frustrated with the performance against Dortmund, said the clash with third-placed City is a great chance to get back to winning ways and shake off any frustration.
"I think these are the best games. I'm really looking forward to it. Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same," Madueke told Amazon Prime.
"We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We're champions, we're at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates.
"There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction."

Rayan Cherki (left) rescued a late draw for Manchester City against Napoli
Manchester City's slick footballing machine is starting to grind to a halt.
The quick passing patterns and edge-of-the-seat action that was evident for so long under former manager Pep Guardiola was supposed to be taken forward by incumbent Enzo Maresca.
It started flawlessly under the Italian with the side winning their first eight games, but that smooth operation is beginning to turn into a turgid and pedestrian showing.
Similar to Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham, moans and groans filled a rather flat Etihad Stadium as the home faithful watched their side labour to a 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli.
City's recent defensive issues also continued, now conceding in 10 successive games and letting in the first goal in seven of those matches.
Maresca said: "We are always looking for three points but when you are not able to win it is important you that don't lose. We take the point, five games [played],10 points and overall I think it is a good result in the end.
"Today, off the ball, once again we didn't concede a lot, the problem is that in this moment they are clinical when we concede a chance, almost every time it is finishing with a goal. We created many chances but in this moment it is like this and move on.
"The first 10 games we always scored first and then in this moment it is exactly in the opposite way, we just need to find a way to avoid that, but I don't think it affects the players in terms of their confidence. We fought until the end."
City were strong favourites for this game and should have had few issues in collecting all three points against a Napoli side that are languishing in eighth place in Serie A.
Their injury issues mean they were able to name only seven substitutes, two of those being goalkeepers, while they had suffered defeat in their past three meetings with City.
They threatened a shock result after twice going ahead through well-taken goals from Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang, but Rayan Cherki managed to salvage a late draw for the hosts.
Maresca's side had 62.7% possession and attempted 665 passes, which largely lacked incisiveness, and of that figure 303 were in the final third compared to Napoli's 77.
The latest disappointing result means City's perfect start is quickly unravelling, now having won only one of their past seven games in all competitions inside 90 minutes.
"It was really surprising to see Manchester City so dull in the first half and so predictable," former Scotland winger Pat Nevin said on BBC Radio 5 Live.
"If you play a team that takes their time, you get yourself set. It is 100% easier to defend.
"You sit and watch City pass, pass, pass, slow, slow. You can get a cigar out."
Star striker Erling Haaland has been in prolific form again this season, scoring 20 goals for club and country, but the 26-year-old has drawn a blank in his past two games.
The Norwegian had chances but failed to score against Fulham on Saturday and though he was handed the captain's armband against Napoli, Haaland was on the periphery for much of the game.
The frontman managed only 14 touches of the ball against the Serie A side on Tuesday, the lowest figure of any player that started the match.
It raises the question whether he is receiving the service to try and find the back of the net.
"I feel I am getting more than enough chances to score," Haaland told TNT Sports. "We tried to push at the end for a goal but we couldn't. Not good enough and we let them in too easy.
"Football is easy and difficult; when you win it's easy and you know what to do, when you don't you start questioning everything. The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy."
City are sixth in the Champions League table, before Wednesday's games, but in the Premier League they have failed to win their past four.
It does not get any easier this weekend, facing a daunting trip to leaders Arsenal on Sunday as they aim to find some form.
Haaland added: "It's the most difficult game of the season going to the champions away.

Florian Wirtz has credited Andoni Iraola with helping him recapture the form that made him one of the most coveted players in Europe when he joined Liverpool in a deal worth up to £116m in 2025.
The Germany international believes he is in the best form of his Liverpool career, having had a difficult debut season under Arne Slot and also struggled in the early weeks of Iraola’s reign. Wirtz scored an exquisite improvised goal in the 4-0 defeat of Manchester United on Sunday when he also created 10 chances from open play.
Speaking in the buildup to Liverpool’s Champions League game against Club Brugge on Wednesday, Wirtz attributed his improvement to becoming “a bit better on a physical level” and gaining a better understanding of English football and the Premier League. The 23-year-old claimed he is back to the heights he reached with Bayer Leverkusen, when Liverpool, Real Madrid and Manchester City all challenged for his services, thanks to working with Iraola.
“I am really enjoying playing under him, he is a really good coach,” said Wirtz in Belgium. “He is bringing me back into the place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football. I can feel that he gives me confidence and I am really happy about that. I am just trying to give him back what he gives me.”
Wirtz has scored five goals in his last four games for club and country, also flourishing on international duty with Jürgen Klopp’s Germany. He said the former Liverpool manager has given him advice on how to prove his worth at Anfield.
The playmaker added: “We speak always about Liverpool when we have the time to do so. He had a great time here. He just tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here, he tries to give me some advice to be successful here because he has shown how it is done. It is small things, more private things. He is just speaking good about the club, the region, the people, and that helps to hear someone who has experienced it.”
Wirtz claimed his fierce self-belief has enabled him to handle criticism since the big-money move from Leverkusen. “It’s mainly a thing that goes on in my own head,” he explained. “It’s not about the people who talk about me. It’s the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself. I always believed in myself. I knew my qualities, and I know them now.
“Sometimes there are phases where you have to work even more to get the output, but I’m just enjoying the moment and really happy that it’s going well. Of course there were days where I wasn’t happy with myself. I always try to work on myself and get better every day but I still believe it makes no sense to put too much pressure on yourself as that doesn’t help in the process to get to where you want. I just believed in myself so I wasn’t too annoyed.”
Liverpool will again be without the injured Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch against Club Brugge , who are second in the Belgian Pro League and won 4-3 at Inter, the Italian champions, last month.
Iraola said: “Sometimes you have to analyse a team and watch a lot of games and it’s a little boring but with Brugge that definitely doesn’t happen. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic. Everyone runs and they are very aggressive in the press. They are coming in on an incredible run of games – 10 wins and a draw in their last 11. We will have to be at a very good level otherwise, it is going to be very difficult.”

Man Utd to contact ProRef and the Premier League over 'totally wrong' interpretation of Leny Yoro's red card in loss at Liverpool after call was overturned; Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino: "What were VAR doing?"; Poch also believes Dominik Szoboszlai’s opener should not have stood
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Mauricio Pochettino has heavily criticised VAR in Manchester United's loss at Liverpool after Leny Yoro's red card was overturned, while the Argentine believes Dominik Szoboszlai’s opener should not have stood.
Yoro's one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in the 4-0 defeat at Anfield has been removed, despite referees' chief Howard Webb supporting the decision to send him off.
Man Utd will contact ProRef and the Premier League directly over what they believe to be a 'totally wrong' interpretation of Yoro's red card against Liverpool.
It is the second time this season VAR has wrongly gone against Man Utd after ProRef admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford in September.
United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision to award Erling Haaland's winner, which was initially ruled offside before VAR overturned the decision.
Pochettino mentioned the Haaland call in a passionate outburst over VAR as he questioned why the VAR did not intervene to overturn the on-field decision.
Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team's Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, Pochettino said: "Very disappointed because I think this type of thing never can happen.
"My question was always the same - we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship with the game.
"But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? No, because now we are going to repeat the game? We're going to have the possibility to play with the similar tools, 11 against 11?
"The problem is that when we were there, I think they need to take their time to review the situation.
"We have an unbelievable car but we need to be in the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way.
"We love and accept the technology, but what are they doing? But it's not only this mistake or the mistake for Haaland against Manchester City, it's how after it affects everything."
Pochettino then insisted that Liverpool's opening goal should not have stood because Bradley Barcola was touching the Manchester United wall as Szoboszlai struck in.
Pochettino referenced a similar call last season, which saw Eberechi Eze's free-kick goal for Crystal Palace at Chelsea disallowed after ex-Palace captain Marc Guehi pushed Moises Caicedo to create a gap for the ball to fly through.
The IFAB Laws of the Game state: "If, when a free-kick is taken, an attacking team player is less than 1 m (1 yd) from a 'wall' formed by three or more defending team players, an indirect free-kick is awarded."
Pochettino believes that the law applied to Szoboszlai's free-kick opener due to Barcola's involvement.
He said: "No one talks about that the goal wasn't legal, it should be disallowed because (Bradley) Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years, they've maybe changed the rule because I've been in America, but last season when (Eberechi) Eze scored for Palace (at Chelsea) you can see [it was disallowed].
"But VAR didn't check [Dominik Szoboszlai's goal]; that must be disallowed.
"But this type of situation, I need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce and to say we were right and the decision wasn't good, and now the three points, where are they?
